Definition: Rabbah, the name of two places in Palestine, East and West
BiblicalUsage: Rabbah is the name of two places in Palestine — the capital of the Ammonites east of the Jordan, and a town in Judah. Joab fought against Rabbah and took the city of waters, and sent to David, 'I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters'; and Moses says Og's bedstead of iron, nine cubits long, was still at Rabbah.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Rabbah marks two endings: the Ammonites' capital fell to David, and the last giant's bed was kept there as a trophy of God's victories.
